DeliveryChannel.description:
Where the work arrives, which is not the same as what shape it is in.

``SubmissionFormat`` answers "what is handed in" — a PDF, a notebook, a
repository. This answers "how does it reach me", and the two are independent:
a notebook can arrive as a Canvas upload or as a pushed commit, and the tools
that can act on it differ completely.

It is a core field rather than an extension because it decides which import
path exists at all. ``lms push`` needs a Canvas assignment id;
``import-graded-exam`` needs the paper question map; an oral defence produces
no artefact for either to attach to, and that is a legitimate state rather
than missing work. The validator checks each channel against the
configuration it implies, which is the whole reason for writing it down.

How hard the professor *intended* an item to be.

Distinct from observed difficulty, which ``ainar score-items`` computes from
what the class actually did. Both are worth having precisely because they
disagree: an item declared ``easy`` that a third of the class fails is either
a badly worded question or a topic that did not land, and neither is visible
from the success rate alone.

One answer option of a choice item.

diagnosis rather than a score.

StudentCapabilityState.description:
What a student can do, accumulated across courses.

Unlike a concept state, this is not scoped to one delivery — a capability
is the thing a transcript cannot express, and evidence for it arrives from
several courses over several years. ``course_version_id`` is set only when the
estimate is deliberately scoped to one run.

There is no confidence field filled in here on purpose. ``source_count``
is the honest signal: a level demonstrated once is not the same claim as a
level demonstrated in four independent places, and inventing a number to
say so would be worse than reporting the count.

All canonical records belonging to one course.

Design-time collections (course, versions, outcomes, concepts,
capabilities, modules, versions, activities, assessments, resources) are

signals, interventions, events, action items) are normally produced by the
application and are empty here unless you are building fixtures.
